crypto.title: Ethereum warns gas changes could break assumptions in existing projects
crypto.summary: Testing for Glamsterdam found projects vulnerable to changes introduced by EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. The Ethereum Foundation warns that revised gas accounting can invalidate assumptions those projects currently rely upon.

crypto.title: Ethereum developers reconsider Hegotá priorities around post-quantum security
crypto.summary: Ethereum developers have dropped quick slots from the current discussion while other consensus choices remain unresolved. The reassessment puts post-quantum resilience ahead of some speed improvements and leaves the upgrade's direction unsettled.

crypto.title: Bitcoin Core discloses block-template failure during transaction reorganization
crypto.summary: Bitcoin Core disclosed a high-severity mempool inconsistency involving TRUC sibling eviction during reorganizations. The issue affects specified older releases and can halt block-template creation; a fix was released in version 30.0.

crypto.title: Bitcoin Core details compact-block processing stall in older releases
crypto.summary: A malicious peer can exploit witness malleation to delay block processing in affected Bitcoin Core versions. The disclosure identifies a medium-severity issue addressed by versions 29.2 and 30.0.

crypto.title: Bitcoin Core fixes unintended whitelist permissions for Tor peers
crypto.summary: Older Bitcoin Core releases could grant inbound Tor peers permissions intended for trusted IP ranges. The disclosure explains how proxy addressing affected whitelist checks and identifies the releases containing fixes.

crypto.title: DOJ targets Binance theft proceeds in North Korea crackdown
crypto.summary: US authorities are pursuing seizure of $1.2 billion linked to the Binance hack. The action accompanies disruption of infrastructure used in a separate North Korean scheme targeting cryptocurrency workers.

crypto.title: North Korean deepfake video calls stole crypto, authorities say
crypto.summary: US authorities attribute more than $400 million in losses to FaceStealer, a scheme impersonating trusted contacts through recorded footage and deepfakes. Victims were tricked into installing malware during purported video calls.

crypto.title: Investigators trace Binance intrusion to repeated fake-interview tactics
crypto.summary: Chainalysis describes how North Korean attackers refined fake employment approaches across multiple operations before the Binance theft. The account connects a major exchange compromise with an established social-engineering playbook.

crypto.title: Chainalysis reports frozen funds after Mercado Bitcoin attack
crypto.summary: Chainalysis says it helped freeze nearly $10 million following a security incident at Mercado Bitcoin. Its account describes a recovery effort after attackers removed assets from the Brazilian exchange.

crypto.title: Chainstack urges customers to rotate credentials after breach
crypto.summary: Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack says customers must replace node credentials and update applications after a data breach. Services remained online, but exposed access information requires action from affected teams.

crypto.title: Trezor tightens reseller network after discovering wallet spy implants
crypto.summary: Trezor reduced its reseller network after finding further spying implants affecting its wallet supply chain. The stricter distribution controls respond to risks introduced before hardware reaches the customer.

crypto.title: Unocoin keeps transfers halted while investigating suspicious wallet activity
crypto.summary: Unocoin continues to suspend deposits and withdrawals while investigating transfers made outside BitGo's platform. BitGo says the freeze worked as intended, leaving the origin of the suspicious signing activity under investigation.

items.title: AWS emulator
items.summary: AWS's official emulator lets developers test service integrations locally without provisioning a cloud account or making paid API calls.
items.paragraph: The emulator exposes AWS-compatible endpoints for the CLI and SDKs, and supports isolated embedded Rust tests. Windows and macOS currently use a container. Service fidelity varies, and the project explicitly excludes production use and security-policy validation.
items.details:
Readers question long-term maintenance and compare existing emulators. Several highlight the difference between API compatibility and testing actual IAM enforcement.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50456631

items.title: Rust 1.100
items.summary: Rust 1.100 stabilizes long-awaited language features and adds Cargo checks that improve dependency hygiene and supply chain controls.
items.paragraph: The release stabilizes the never type and allocator APIs, alongside standard-library additions. Cargo can report unused dependencies and enforce a minimum publication age for newly selected versions. These changes affect both language expressiveness and routine dependency management.
items.details:
Discussion emphasizes custom allocators, unused-dependency warnings, and dependency cooldowns. Readers also point to useful standard-library additions beyond the headline features.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50472038

items.title: A false smoke alarm almost drowned Jane Street's only NYC datacenter
items.summary: A former Jane Street engineer recounts how a false alarm disabled cooling and threatened a trading firm's datacenter.
items.paragraph: The incident exposed interactions between smoke detection, cooling, and fire suppression. Engineers rushed to remove power before rising temperatures triggered sprinklers. The account illustrates why physical failure modes belong in reliability planning.
items.details:
Readers compare hurricane-era datacenter emergencies and question the absence of coordinated emergency power controls. Others discuss the operational burden placed on staff living nearby.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50455394

items.title: Gemini Decisions API
items.summary: Google's Decisions API scores bounded questions across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs without generating a conventional response.
items.paragraph: Gemini Decision 1 returns probabilities for yes/no questions, choices, and rubric scores. A request can include multiple questions about the same input. The interface targets routing, filtering, policy checks, and other decisions embedded in applications.
items.details:
Readers welcome multimodal inputs while debating calibration and comparisons with Jev. Discussion distinguishes scored choices from merely asking a generative model to state confidence.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50456791

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.summary: Google introduces Gemini 4 Hydrogen for faster coding and agent execution, extending its latest model family across developer products.
items.paragraph: Hydrogen targets the repeatable execution work inside larger agent workflows. Google is rolling it out through its API, AI Studio, consumer products, and Antigravity. The release includes a million-token context window and adjustable reasoning effort.
items.details:
Readers discuss the immediate rollout and find the new model names difficult to compare. Questions focus on positioning and practical speed rather than headline rankings.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50471431

items.title: I'm making LLMs work on small and old devices
items.summary: Smolmaxxing runs language models on old phones and TV boxes by combining device-specific kernels with flash-backed weight streaming.
items.paragraph: The project publishes measurements from a TV box, an older iPad, and an Android phone. It keeps only part of a model in RAM and streams other weights from storage. The work explores local inference on hardware usually considered too constrained for these models.
items.details:
The project drew substantial interest in reusing limited hardware for local inference. Discussion is linked below for device-specific experiences.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50468888

items.title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server
items.summary: A critical Apache HTTP Server flaw can allow remote code execution through a race condition in its HTTP/2 module.
items.paragraph: The reported vulnerability affects shared header handling in mod_http2. Concurrent requests can trigger heap corruption in the server process. The disclosure makes version and configuration review a priority for operators of affected servers.
items.details:
Readers examine the patch and debate the complexity introduced by HTTP/2. Some compare Apache's continued deployment with newer server alternatives.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50462177

items.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
items.summary: Edge0 releases large local models and an inference stack aimed at running agent workloads on comparatively constrained personal hardware.
items.paragraph: The release combines sparse expert architectures with low-precision weights and deployment tooling. The publisher reports local coding and reasoning examples and provides artifacts for reproduction. Hardware requirements and performance claims need to be evaluated against the actual workload.
items.details:
Readers are interested in memory savings and tool-use demonstrations. Others question how much novelty comes from the underlying model and whether generated designs remain editable.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50475713

items.title: Ggml v1.0.0
items.summary: GGML reaches version 1.0 with backend improvements and clearer compatibility boundaries for applications embedding local machine learning inference.
items.paragraph: The tensor library underpins llama.cpp and other local AI software. This release includes changes across CPU and accelerator backends, along with scheduling and distributed execution work. The versioned library interface matters to downstream integrators.
items.details:
Users describe performance improvements on existing hardware and emphasize support for less common GPUs. Several see the library as core infrastructure for local inference.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50493062

items.title: After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models
items.summary: Hundreds of experiments explore how planning and subgoals affect JEPA world models without requiring additional model training.
items.paragraph: The author tests a latent-space model on block-pushing tasks and examines why longer plans fail. Breaking tasks into subgoals improves the planner while leaving the predictor unchanged. Interactive examples make the distinction between model accuracy and planning strategy concrete.
items.details:
Readers compare the approach with model predictive control and hierarchical planning. They question demonstration-derived goals and distinguish useful experimentation from claims of novelty.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50487185

items.title: Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG
items.summary: Apple explores learned retrieval methods that use typical query distributions to improve search efficiency in recommendation and RAG systems.
items.paragraph: Small neural networks are trained offline for a fixed set of candidate vectors. They learn how to route likely queries toward relevant candidates instead of relying only on geometric partitions. The approach trades preparation cost for better retrieval at serving time.
items.details:
Commenters debate where learned routing justifies its complexity. Several contrast hyperscale retrieval with smaller systems where lexical search or direct agent exploration may suffice.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50455633

items.title: Atuin Threads: All your agent sessions on every machine
items.summary: Atuin Threads makes agent sessions searchable and resumable across tools and machines, using an opt-in encrypted synchronization workflow.
items.paragraph: The feature extends Atuin's history model to agent conversations and their execution context. Sessions can move between supported harnesses, while an MCP interface lets agents search earlier work. Users can keep the data local or use hosted or self-managed sync.
items.details:
Readers compare alternative memory tools and question whether every experimental session deserves retention. One reports an unrelated filesystem-error handling issue with Atuin.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50453637

items.title: Turning a 22-year-old Postgres type-confusion primitive into RCE
items.summary: A PostgreSQL investigation shows how stale type assumptions can turn authenticated database access into a memory-corruption vulnerability.
items.paragraph: The researcher follows composite values and schema changes into PostgreSQL's internal type representation. The case connects extension research with a flaw in the core database. Its practical significance is strongest where database privileges must remain isolated from host execution.
items.details:
Discussion stresses the authenticated-access requirement and argues for clearer privilege-escalation terminology. Readers summarize the invalidation problem behind the longer investigation.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50471761

items.title: Relax: JIT compiler for Rust to reduce build times
items.summary: Relax experiments with compiling Rust functions on demand and patching live processes to shorten the development feedback loop.
items.paragraph: The JIT runtime aims to start Cargo packages directly from source and compile functions when called. It is explicitly experimental and has mostly been tested in Makepad's own workflows. Conventional Rust release builds remain the recommended shipping path.
items.details:
Early testers report compatibility failures and mixed performance. Others welcome renewed attention to interactive development while comparing it with older live-programming systems.
Discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50458849

items.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.summary: XYBench tests whether assistants identify the underlying problem behind a user’s question instead of reinforcing a mistaken premise.
items.paragraph: Allen AI’s benchmark contains 8,115 questions designed around cases where the requested solution may not solve the real problem. This matters for assistants used in debugging and support, where following instructions literally can deepen the original mistake.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.summary: IBM introduces model-native markup in Granite to distinguish structured instructions and data more explicitly during language model interactions.
items.paragraph: LLMON introduces reserved tokens and a structured markup format supported by Granite 4.1 3B and 8B. It gives models explicit boundaries for content that ordinary text formatting leaves ambiguous. That is relevant to prompt injection defenses and reliable tool interactions, although format support alone does not establish complete protection.

items.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.summary: Amazon’s expert-pruning method considers cooperating expert pairs to reduce mixture-of-experts memory use while preserving more of the model’s capabilities.
items.paragraph: HOPE selects experts for removal using pairwise interactions rather than scoring each expert independently. The article explains why deleting one member of a cooperating pair can cause more damage than its individual score suggests. It includes instructions for applying the method and publisher evaluations comparing quality at different pruning levels.

items.title: Decision Models in Hugging Face
items.summary: Hugging Face documents decision models and their integrations for applications needing structured choices rather than open-ended generated answers.
items.paragraph: Decision models turn application questions into bounded outputs such as choices or scores. The article describes the emerging model category and its place in Hugging Face tooling. This is useful for routing and classification systems that need a defined output contract and a way to handle uncertainty.

items.title: Workflow SDK 5: built for production

items.paragraph: The release builds on Vercel’s reported four billion workflow steps and 700 million runs. It encrypts workflow payloads before they leave application code, using a separate key for each run. The changes address a central operational concern: durable event logs can contain credentials, customer information, and model context.

items.title: Vercel Sandbox starts up to 4x faster

items.title: Daemons can now send traces to Vercel Tracing

items.title: Vercel Security Review no longer requires a linked Vercel project

items.paragraph: The article explains the design of a specialized language for expressing parallel work. Its focus is making efficient execution easier to express within the OxCaml environment. The examples connect the abstraction to the implementation constraints that motivated it.
